questions.question: Which letter lies exactly between H and P in the English alphabet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First letter = H

Last letter = P

**Calculation:**

Position of H = 8

Position of P = 16

⇒ Middle position = (8 + 16)

24/2 = 12

12th letter = L

**∴ L lies exactly between H and P.**

questions.question: The seminar in Nashik was held 2 days after the one in Surat. Indore's seminar was 3 days before the one in Surat. If the seminar in Indore was on 8th April, when did the seminar in Nashik happen?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Indore seminar = 8 April

Indore = 3 days before Surat

Nashik = 2 days after Surat

**Formula used:**

Surat Date = Indore Date + 3 days

Nashik Date = Surat Date + 2 days

**Calculation:**

Surat Date

⇒ 8 April + 3 days = 11 April

Nashik Date

⇒ 11 April + 2 days = 13 April

**∴ Seminar in Nashik was held on 13 April.**

questions.question:
What should come in place of the question mark '?' in the following number series?

9, 14, 24, 39, 59, ?, 114
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Series: 9, 14, 24, 39, 59, ?, 114

**Formula used:**

Pattern: Increasing by +5, +10, +15, +20, +25, +30

**Calculation:**

14 − 9 = 5

24 − 14 = 10

39 − 24 = 15

59 − 39 = 20

Next increase = 25

⇒ ? = 59 + 25 = 84

Check:

114 − 84 = 30 ✔

**∴ Missing number = 84**

questions.question:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Decide which of the given conclusions is/are definitely TRUE from the statement.

Statement: P > Q T = R ≥ U > V

Conclusion I: V T

options.text: Both Conclusion I and Conclusion II are True
Neither Conclusion I nor Conclusion II is True

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Statement: P > Q T = R ≥ U > V

**Formula used:**

Basic inequality chain comparison

**Calculation:**

P > Q

S > Q

S > T

T = R

R ≥ U

U > V

⇒ S > T = R ≥ U > V

⇒ S > V

⇒ V Q and S > T

No direct relation between P and T

⇒ P > T cannot be determined ✘

**Conclusion II is NOT definitely TRUE.**

**∴ Only Conclusion I is TRUE.**

questions.question:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement:

Some cats are dogs.All dogs are animals.

Conclusions:

I. Some cats are animals.

II. All cats are animals.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Some cats are dogs

All dogs are animals

**Formula used:**

Some A are B + All B are C ⇒ Some A are C

**Calculation:**

Some cats are dogs

All dogs ⊂ animals

⇒ Some cats are animals ✔

But no statement says All cats are dogs

⇒ All cats are animals ✘

**∴ Only Conclusion I follows.**

questions.question: The price of an item first increases by 20% and then decreases by 20% from the new price. What is the net percentage change in the original price of the item?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Increase = 20%

Decrease = 20%

**Formula used:**

Net % change = a − b − (a × b)/(100) 

**Calculation:**

a = 20, b = 20

⇒ Net % = 20 − 20 − (20 × 20)/(100) 

⇒ Net % = 0 − 4

⇒ −4%

**∴ Net change = 4% decrease.**

questions.question: If @ = -, % = x, # = +; then 10 % 2 @ 4 # 3 = ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

@ = −

% = ×

# = +

Expression: 10 % 2 @ 4 # 3

**Formula used:**

BODMAS rule

**Calculation:**

10 % 2 @ 4 # 3

⇒ 10 × 2 − 4 + 3

⇒ 20 − 4 + 3

⇒ 16 + 3

⇒ 19

**∴ Answer = 19**

questions.question: Statements: Some stars are planets. Some planets are moons. Conclusions: I. Some moons are stars. II. All planets being stars is a possibility.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Statements: Some stars are planets. Some planets are moons.

Conclusions: I. Some moons are stars. II. All planets being stars is a possibility.

**Formula used:**

Syllogism Rules (Venn Diagram Method)

**Calculation:**

**For Conclusion I:**

⇒ Stars and Moons have no direct connection in the basic diagram.

⇒ Conclusion I is "False" (Not a definite follow).

**For Conclusion II:**

⇒ Statement says "Some stars are planets".

⇒ In a possible case, the set of Planets can be entirely inside the set of Stars.

⇒ This does not contradict the given statements.

⇒ Conclusion II is "True" (Possibility exists).

**∴ Only conclusion II follows.**
